perMutant.note: found only with synthesis on: the drain needs a NEW output (the attacker's payment box at the sale's price position) while the stock returns to the sale box — out of phase-1's fixed output set CONFOUNDED: the same drainable verdict fires on the unmutated original (see escalatedFindings) — the hunt's objective has no attacker-cost accounting, so overpayment probes score as drains. The real 1-nanoERG drain IS in family (710 hits), but the verdict alone cannot discriminate.

perMutant.missDetail: the witness moves the bank NFT out of the successor's tokens(0) (a junk token takes its slot): a token-LAYOUT variation of a FIXED output. No synthesis degree re-pads a template output — only companion RE-CREATIONS get padding. The phase-1 fixed shape cannot express it either.

the witness re-trees the pool SUCCESSOR (a fixed output) to the attacker's script with reserves intact: drain mode re-trees only the FREE payee, and no synthesis degree modifies a template output's tree. Same missing axis as M5: fixed-output re-pad/re-tree.

same missing axis as M6, on the incident's own fixed contract: the swap successor must be re-treed to steal the locked order value. The hunt spends 29,448 probes in family and misses — the axis, not the budget, is the gap.

out-of-family: M7 — one missing probe axis: re-pad / re-tree a FIXED (template) output. Phase-3 backlog entry #1; would likely convert all three.
keyed-insider (out of attacker model): M3 — residuals require the beneficiary's/receiver's key; the hunt refuses needsProof on protected inputs by contract. A keyed-insider hunt is a phase-3+ attacker-model extension, not a coverage fix.

negativeControls.escalated: see escalatedFindings - the firing is recorded, the fixture untouched

escalatedFindings.what: the winning probe has the attacker OVERPAY the seller (20M of the attacker's own nanoERG into the seller's P2PK box) so `paid` passes legitimately and the stock leaves the sale box with it. The seller is fully paid; the attacker loses money. No exploit.
escalatedFindings.why: the leak objective counts protected value that LEFT the protected box, sanctioned only at the free payee's DECLARED amounts, and never subtracts what the attacker SPENT. An overpayment that empties a protected box into a protocol-designated payee scores as a drain.
escalatedFindings.disposition: ESCALATED, not fixed: attacker-cost accounting is the roadmap's parked 'pricing / worth-weighted objectives; economic probes — separate spec' (phase 2 spec, non-goals). This firing is the concrete evidence for that spec. The fixture is untouched.
escalatedFindings.consequence: M4's `found` is confounded: the mutant IS really exploitable (the 1-nanoERG purchase is a genuine keyless theft and is in family — the hunt scored 710 hits), but its drainable verdict cannot be distinguished from overpayment noise without a cost-aware objective. Recorded as found=true, confounded=true.

negativeControlsNote: every original runs in both configurations, asserted in the harness; a drainable original must be pre-recorded in escalatedFindings (M4) or the run fails. Six of seven originals are clean; M4's firing is the corpus's escalated finding.

knownDetectableControl.what: delete-nft-check applied to examples/incidents/fixed/use-lp-swap.es reconstructs the DEPLOYED vulnerable useLpSwap (both halves of the NFT binding deleted - exactly what the deployed contract lacked). Ground truth: it drained 284,695 ERG on mainnet at height 1,868,204.
knownDetectableControl.expected: drainable from the honest shape (synthesis off - phase 1 rediscovers it)
knownDetectableControl.note: a pass/fail on the APPARATUS, reported separately - never a corpus mutant, never in the rate's denominator (a found control would move the rate without the hunt changing). Landing this control caught a fixture bug in the control's own template (the swap successor initially lacked the swap NFT, failing swapSucc.tokens == SELF.tokens on every probe) - the control doing its job.

detectionRateNote: attributable detections / proven mutants. A drainable verdict counts only when the mutant's own unmutated control is CLEAN in the same configuration — a hit that also fires on the original says nothing about the mutation. Derived by the harness, not flagged by hand.
foundNote: raw drainable verdicts on proven mutants: see rawDrainableOnProven (1, all confounded)
